bull.b: Rapid quarterly revenue growth, a rising backlog, and a sizable commercial pipeline provide evidence of improving customer demand and sales execution. If the company converts advanced opportunities and booked orders, higher utilization of its platform could support sustained growth over the next several quarters.

Growing consumables revenue strengthens the installed-base economics of SteraMist by adding usage-linked sales beyond one-time equipment purchases. This recurring component can improve revenue visibility, deepen customer engagement, and support more durable gross-profit generation as deployments expand.

Additional regulatory approvals and international authorizations broaden the applications and geographies available to TOMI’s technology. Combined with major customer wins and distribution progress, this expands the addressable market and creates more pathways for the platform to gain institutional adoption.

bear.b: TOMI has not yet translated its solid gross margin into sustainable operating or net profitability. Continued losses reduce internal funding capacity and make future earnings dependent on substantial revenue growth, expense control, and successful conversion of the company’s pipeline.

Persistent operating cash burn and elevated leverage weaken financial flexibility even as reported equity remains positive. The company may need continued external financing to fund operations and growth, increasing exposure to refinancing pressure, dilution, and constraints on strategic investment.

Important expansion opportunities remain contingent on regulatory approvals that can take time and may not arrive as planned. In parallel, the pending merger’s minimum financing condition adds execution uncertainty, potentially delaying strategic benefits or increasing the company’s capital requirements.
